text:
Predicates:
AllowedIn(x, y) ::: Pets are allowed in building y.
DepositRequired(x, y) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building y.
EqualOrMore(x, y) ::: The deposit can be either equal to or more than y.
CanRent(x, y) ::: x can rent an apartment in y.
HasPet(x, y) ::: x has pet y.
Pet(y) ::: y is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(y) ::: y is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(y, z) ::: The monthly rent in building y is z.
WillRent(x, y) ::: x will rent an apartment in y.
MoveInWithPet(x, y) ::: x can move in with pet y.
Premises:
Pets are allowed in some managed buildings. ::: AllowedIn(Pet(y), y) ∧ ManagedBuilding(y)
A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building. ::: DepositRequired(x, y)
The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more. ::: EqualOrMore(deposit, monthlyRent(y))
Fluffy is Tom's cat. ::: Pet(Fluffy) ∧ HasPet(Tom, Fluffy)
Cats are pets. ::: Pet(Cat)
The Olive Garden is a managed building. ::: ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden)
The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000. ::: MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000)
Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500. ::: WillRent(Tom, oliveGarden) ↔ (MoveInWithPet(Tom, Fluffy) ∧ Deposit ≤ 1500)
2000 is more than 1500. ::: 2000 > 1500
Conclusion:
The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more. ::: ∃d (Deposit(oliveGarden, d) ∧ (d ≥ 2000))
